findings.statement: Create a new OAuth2 application under workspace Settings > API > OAuth applications, then configure redirect callback URLs; a dedicated workspace is recommended for managing it, since every admin in that workspace gets access to the app.
findings.excerpt: each admin user will have access

findings.statement: Scopes are a comma-separated list on the authorize request: read is the default, write/issues:create/comments:create/timeSchedule:write are narrower options, and admin ('full access to admin level endpoints') should never be requested unless it's absolutely needed.
Access tokens expire after 24 hours; refreshing returns a new access token and refresh token, with a 30-minute grace period to replay the original refresh request if a network error occurs.

Adding actor=app to the authorization URL makes the app itself perform mutations (creating issues, comments, status changes) instead of the authenticating user - useful for agents and service accounts; a custom display name can still be set via createAsUser.

Linear's Integration Directory lists apps Linear builds plus third-party integrations; it accepts apps it considers useful to the community and built by formal companies, generally turning away scripts and hobbyist apps.
Submitting to the Integration Directory starts with filling out a form, then sending assets to integrations@linear.app.
Composio offers a managed OAuth app for Linear by default; a custom auth config (your own Linear OAuth app) is for your own branding, scopes, rate limits, or production use.
Linear also supports an API key as an alternative to OAuth.

findings.statement: Linear's OAuth scopes are: read (default, always present), write, issues:create, comments:create, timeSchedule:write, and admin (full access to admin-level endpoints - never request unless absolutely needed); two further agent-specific scopes, app:assignable and app:mentionable, are undescribed on this page and documented separately for App authentication.

tierReason.text: Linear's OAuth docs describe a fully self-serve app-creation flow with no review, security assessment, or partner requirement of any kind.

scopeForks.text: Submitting to Linear's optional Integration Directory (for public discoverability) isn't a technical review - Linear says it accepts integrations useful to the community and built by formal companies, generally turning away scripts and hobbyist apps. This doesn't block using your OAuth app directly; it only affects whether it's listed in the directory.

claim.text: Composio offers a managed OAuth app for Linear by default, so a developer can skip registering their own.

whatYouLose.text: On a managed app, the consent screen shows the platform's name and brand instead of yours, and scopes/rate limits are typically fixed rather than something you control.

whenToSwitch.text: Switch to your own Linear OAuth app once you need your own branding, specific scopes, or your own rate limits.

flow.text: A developer creates an OAuth2 application, chooses scopes, and users authorize it through Linear's standard OAuth flow; adding actor=app lets the app perform mutations itself instead of the authorizing user.

appTypes.text: By default, API actions are attributed to the authenticating user; actor=app switches attribution to the app itself, intended for agents and service accounts.

tokenNotes.text: Access tokens expire after 24 hours and must be refreshed; a refresh has a 30-minute grace period to retry on a network error.
